### Findings

**MEDIUM — `credit_string` silently mangles a credit when one part has no source, and the release is not counted incomplete.**
`src/discography/musicbrainz.rs:303-314`. The name falls back to `""` for a part with neither a credit-level `name` nor an `artist` entity, but the `joinphrase` is appended unconditionally. Scenario: payload `"artist-credit": [{"name":"Nu:Tone","joinphrase":" & "},{"joinphrase":" & "},{"name":"Stamina MC"}]` (an anonymous middle part) yields `"Nu:Tone && Stamina MC"`, which then becomes the Soulseek search artist and the staging folder name (`label_discover.rs:163-175` → `runner.rs:2770-2792`). A trailing anonymous part yields `"Nu:Tone &"` instead. This contradicts the function's own comment ("a part with neither source contributes nothing") and the round-3 requirement that such a part makes the release incomplete; only an *entirely* empty credit is rejected (`musicbrainz.rs:324-326`). Smallest fix: append `joinphrase` only when `name` is non-empty, and treat a part with no source as a reason to return `None` from `from_wire` (count it `incomplete`); add the missing unit test (no test covers an anonymous part, with or without a joinphrase).

**MEDIUM — the label entry point and the dispatch branch are completely untested.**
`src/runner.rs:2548-2585` (`run_label_discover_mode`) is never called by any test, and neither is the `labels.is_empty()` branch in `src/main.rs:606-621`. Grep shows the only references are `main.rs:614` and the definition. Consequences: (a) an inverted or wrong guard on `labels.is_empty()` would silently run the artist sweep instead of the label sweep and no test would fail — the clap test (`main.rs:899-935`) and the plan test (`mode.rs:1290-1305`) stop short of dispatch; (b) the label-specific preconditions (`discography.enabled`, `library.paths`, `staging::prepare`) are unexercised; (c) this code is uncovered for the project's 95% line-coverage gate. Smallest fix: one `#[tokio::test]` in `main.rs` that dispatches `ExecutionPlan::Discover { labels: vec![LabelRequest{..}], .. }` with empty `library.paths` and asserts the label-specific text "a label sweep needs a library to check what is present" (`runner.rs:2564`) — it fails today if the branch is ever inverted, because the artist branch says "needs a library to derive artists from".

**MEDIUM — the round-3 invariant "a malformed refusal cannot suppress a later corrected run" has no test.**
`src/discography/label.rs:1153-1177` asserts only `search_calls == 0`, `from_cache == false` and the reason. Nothing asserts that no `discography_failures` row was written for the key and that a subsequent valid input still resolves. The behaviour is correct today (`label.rs:328-340` returns before the only writer at `label.rs:422`), but the property the review round asked for is exactly the one a future refactor (e.g. moving the guard below the replay) would break with no red test. Smallest fix: after the refusal, assert `db.get_discography_failure(&input.cache_key()).unwrap().is_none()`, then run `Input::parse("<correct UUID>")` against the same DB and assert a `Catalogue`.

**LOW — a malformed value is reported as a MusicBrainz resolution failure.**
`src/discography/label.rs:331-336` returns `kind: DiscoveryFailure::Unresolved`, so `runner.rs:2693-2703` logs "label could not be resolved on MusicBrainz: …" for a value that provably never went to MusicBrainz, pushes it into `counters.unresolved`, and (with a second unresolved label) prints "pin … with discography.label_mbids" (`label_discover.rs:288-297`) — advice that cannot work, because the guard runs before the pin is read. Unreachable from the binary (`mode.rs:82-99` refuses it), so this is a library-caller contract blemish only.

**LOW — README overstates the malformed-UUID shape rule.**
`README.md:221`: "four hyphen-separated hexadecimal groups within three characters of a UUID's 32 digits". `looks_like_mbid` (`src/discography/label.rs:138-151`) requires exactly four hyphens / **five** groups (8-4-4-4-12) and a stripped length of `30..=34`, i.e. within **two** digits. The refusal message itself is correct ("8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal digits"); the parenthetical should match it.

**LOW — a label run cancelled before its first label prints an empty summary.**
`runner.rs:2620-2631` returns through `finish_label_run` before `labels_examined` is incremented, and every notice in `label_notices` is conditional (`label_discover.rs:261,273,280,315,345,361`), so the run emits zero summary lines. `discover_notices` deliberately avoids exactly this ("A run that examined no artist at all would be silent otherwise", `discover.rs:754-766`). Smallest fix: emit the "`N` of `M` label(s) examined" line unconditionally (it reads honestly as `0 of 1`), plus a unit test for the all-default `LabelCounters`.

**LOW — the label core function drops the preconditions its artist twin repeats.**
`run_label_discover_mode_with_provider` (`runner.rs:2590-2601`) starts at `let allowed = …`, while `run_discover_mode_with_provider` re-checks `discography.enabled` and `library.paths` (`runner.rs:3080-3089`) even though its public wrapper already did. No current bug, but the two core entry points now disagree about whether they are safe to call directly, and the next caller inherits a silent half-configured run.

**LOW — the label run summary is undocumented.**
The README documents the `discover:` notice format in several places but has no description of the `label:` lines emitted by `label_notices` (`label_discover.rs:258-370`), nor does the `--label` row (`README.md:221`) state that a label sweep requires `discography.enabled: true` and a non-empty `library.paths` — both are enforced at `runner.rs:2557-2567`.

### Note for the supervisor (cannot be run here)

Please run `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and the coverage gate (`cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 95`) before merging: finding 2 is partly a coverage-gate risk and none of these gates was executable in this review.

########## B ##########
### Findings

1. **MEDIUM — missing cancellation tests for the new label sweep.**
   `src/runner.rs` label test block (~:7040-7700). The sweep has three cancellation-sensitive exits — the between-labels poll (src/runner.rs:2620-2631), the scan-cancelled `finish_label_run` (:2737-2742) and the download-loop break (:2783-2785) — and none is exercised. The crate already has three cancellation tests for artist-only mode (`a_cancelled_scan_stops_a_legacy_artist_only_run`, `a_cancelled_scan_stops_an_artist_only_run_without_processing_an_album`, `authoritative_cancellation_stops_iteration`). Concrete failure: a plausible refactor that folds the cancel `break` into the budget-exhausted branch would set `budget_reached_at` on a user-interrupted run — precisely the false "budget reached" notice the artist sweep carries a comment against (runner.rs:3305-3310) — and CI would stay green. Smallest fix: one test per exit — a client that flips a shared flag after the first search (the existing `CancelAfterFirstSearchClient` pattern) driving `run_label_discover_mode_with_provider`, asserting no "budget reached" notice, the honest examined line, and no staging claims; plus an `Err(Cancelled)` result from `index_from_paths` (needs a stubbed scanner or an `AtomicBool` pre-set to true).

2. **MEDIUM — the whole-library scan is paid (and can abort) for a run that can stage nothing.**
   `src/runner.rs:2719-2755`. Selection and counters are computed *before* the scan, but the scan is unconditional. When `selection.targets` is empty (all catalogues filtered out by `--release-type`, or bounded out by `--since`: a very plausible invocation — "sweep label X, but only EPs" or "--since 2024" on a label that stopped releasing in 1990), the run still performs its longest phase — the full tag-scanning walk — only to count `present = 0` for zero targets, and a scan failure (unreadable root, `Err` at :2748-2754) then turns a run with no possible work into a nonzero exit. Skipping the walk when `selection.targets.is_empty()` removes the waste and the spurious error with no honesty change: present/missing/eligible all stay truthful at zero. (No information is lost — `present` can only count targets, and there are none.)

3. **LOW — `credit_string` can append a dangling joinphrase for a pathological payload.**
   `src/discography/musicbrainz.rs:295-314`. An entry carrying a `joinphrase` but *neither* a credit-level name *nor* an artist entity contributes only its joinphrase, so a credit assembled from such entries can become e.g. `"feat. X"` — non-empty, so `from_wire` keeps the release and it is matched under a string that names no artist, rather than being counted incomplete. Unreachable with real MusicBrainz payloads (every credit entry always carries `artist`); the struct is already defensive, so defend the same corner: drop a part's joinphrase when the part contributed no name (or count any part with no source as making the release incomplete). File the same caveat for `{"artist": {}}` (entity present, empty name).

4. **LOW — README wording for the malformed-ID rule is ambiguous.**
   `README.md` (`--label` CLI row, diff around line 221): "a value hyphenated like a MusicBrainz ID that is not one (four hyphen-separated hexadecimal groups within three characters of a UUID's 32 digits)". `looks_like_mbid` (src/discography/label.rs:138-150) requires *four hyphens* separating *five* groups of hex digits; the parenthetical can be misread as four groups. The runtime message already says it precisely ("8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal digits"). Suggest "four hyphens separating five hexadecimal groups within three characters of a UUID's 32 digits".

5. **LOW — README does not say `discover.exclude_artists` applies to label sweeps.**
   `README.md` label paragraph/`--label` row. The code applies exclusion to credit keys and counts them (`label_targets(..., &config.discover.exclude_artists)`, src/runner.rs:2723; notice at label_discover.rs:330-333), and the committed spec documents it (spec line 151-152), but the README never mentions it for `--label`. One sentence ("`discover.exclude_artists` still applies to credits") closes it.

6. **LOW — the "incomplete MusicBrainz data" notice is not selection-gated.**
   `src/label_discover.rs:324-327` vs the `selection_ran` gate at :345. On a run aborted in the label loop *after* a cached/fresh catalogue carried incomplete payloads, the printed line reads "N release(s) skipped: incomplete MusicBrainz data" even though no selection/skipping ever happened — the count is truthful (byte-accurate about the payload) but "skipped" is a selection word applied to a discarded run. Either re-worm it ("payload could not describe N release(s)") or gate it with `selection_ran`. Cosmetic honesty nit; everything else in the aborted-run report is accurate.

### Merge verdict

**Finding: HIGH — an interrupted album is still counted, budget‑charged and reported as a failure; the `Err(SeakarrError::Cancelled)` arm that was supposed to prevent this is unreachable.**
Location: `src/runner.rs:2820-2845` (Ok arm `2821-2831`, Err arm `2834-2842`).

Evidence: `SeakarrError::Cancelled` is constructed in exactly one place, the library walk (`src/scanner.rs:327`; declared `src/error.rs:27`). `process_album` never walks the library, so it can never return that variant. A Ctrl+C during a download arrives as `SeakarrError::Download("download cancelled by user")` (`src/download.rs:193, 204, 437, 473, 492, 848, 952, 1408`), which `download_ranked_candidates` deliberately swallows into `Ok(DownloadStage::Failed { outcome: AlbumOutcome::Failed { reason } })` (`runner.rs:1404-1440`), and `process_album` then returns `Ok(outcome)` (`runner.rs:706-708`).

Failure scenario: `seakarr --mode discover --label "Hospital Records"` with ten missing albums; the operator presses Ctrl+C while album 3 downloads.
1. `Ok(AlbumOutcome::Failed { reason: "download cancelled by user" })` → `charges_download_budget` is true for `Failed` (`runner.rs:2329-2334`) → `budget.charge()`;
2. `count_label_outcome` → `failed_albums += 1` (`runner.rs:2874-2887`);
3. `report.record(..., AlbumOutcome::Failed { .. })` → the summary prints `Failed (1): … download cancelled by user`;
4. next iteration sees the flag and sets `counters.cancelled = true`, so the summary reads `… 0 album(s) staged; 1 failed` plus `cancelled by user`.

So the operator is told the run failed an album it merely interrupted, `discover.max_cycle_downloads` loses one slot permanently (scheduled runs download one fewer album), and the round‑6 claim ("an interrupted album is no longer counted or reported as a failure") does not hold. Secondary aggravating detail: the budget check precedes the cancel check (`runner.rs:2798-2804`), so when the interrupted album's charge exhausts the budget the run reports `budget … reached` rather than `cancelled` — the exact conflation the artist sweep's comment at `runner.rs:3271-3275` warns about.

Smallest fix: in the `Ok(outcome)` arm, treat a failure whose reason says so as a cancellation, using the idiom already in the tree (`runner.rs:1836-1839`):
`if matches!(&outcome, AlbumOutcome::Failed { reason } if reason.contains("cancelled by user")) { counters.cancelled = true; break; }` — before charging, counting or recording. (Checking the flag alone would also convert a real failure that coincides with an interrupt, so match the reason.) Add a regression test (see next finding).

**Finding: MEDIUM — no test covers cancellation during an album, which is why the HIGH defect passed six rounds.**
Location: label test block `src/runner.rs:7420-7935`; cancel tests are only `a_cancelled_label_run_stops_before_the_first_label` (`runner.rs:7760`) and `cancellation_after_the_first_label_stops_the_sweep` (`runner.rs:7869`, which drives the between‑labels poll via `CancellingProvider`, `runner.rs:7795`).

Nothing exercises the pre‑album poll (`runner.rs:2802-2804`) or the outcome/error routes of an interrupted album, and `count_label_outcome`'s unit test (`runner.rs:7487`) asserts the very behaviour that is wrong for a cancellation. The spec's correction block (spec:449-460) claims the album path is handled. Smallest fix: one test that sets the flag inside the download stage (e.g. a `MockClient` whose write trips the flag, or a `process_album` result injected as `Failed { reason: "download cancelled by user" }`) asserting `staged_albums == 0`, `failed_albums == 0`, `cancelled == true`, and no `Failed (…)` entry in the report.

**Finding: LOW — `--label "mbid:<uuid>"` is accepted as a label *name* and aliases the ID's cache/failure key.**

Scenario: a peer advertises `01 - cancelled by user.flac`, never accepts the transfer, the default 1800 s queue deadline expires → `AlbumOutcome::Failed { reason: "...cancelled by user.flac..." }` → `outcome_is_cancellation` is true → the label sweep stops, reports "cancelled by user", exits 0, and the album is never counted or recorded. The unit test only pins two strings, so this false positive is untested. Smallest fix: carry a typed cancellation signal (or match the exact reason `"download cancelled by user"`), and add a `Failed` reason embedding the phrase as a negative test. content.text:
## Summary of changes on branch `main`

**What this delivers** — a new **label-based discovery** capability for `discover` mode: `--label` sweeps a record label instead of your library, `--release-type` picks the wanted categories, and `--since` bounds the sweep by first-release-date.

- **Two new modules.** `src/discography/label.rs` owns label identity (name or MusicBrainz label ID, resolved with the same exact-match and score-dominance rules as artists, pinnable via `discography.label_mbids`), and the 30-day cached catalogue fetched by browsing the label's official releases with pagination guards and a 5000-release ceiling. `src/label_discover.rs` is pure selection: merge labels, filter by type and `--since`, reuse the existing bundle/identity logic, dedupe, and order deterministically.
- **Provider work.** Three new `DiscographyProvider` methods (label search, label lookup, official-release catalogue), with credit strings built from MusicBrainz's own names and joinphrases, incomplete releases counted rather than guessed, and a 404 mapped to "unresolved" so a mistyped ID cannot trip the outage breaker.
- **Runner work.** A label sweep that validates every request up front, fetches one catalogue per label, walks the library once, and downloads only into staging — a label run never writes into your library. Cancellation is honoured between labels, between albums and mid-download; an interrupted album is never charged or reported as a failure. It reports a `label:` notice block covering resolution, drops, presence, staging and the budget, and shares the artist sweep's circuit-breaker logic rather than a copy of it.
- **CLI and config.** `--label`, `--release-type` and `--since` on `discover`, with every cross-mode conflict refused explicitly; `discography.label_mbids` pins with validation shared with `artist_mbids`.
- **Tests and docs.** Coverage rose from 92% to 96% on the new provider module; 1535 tests pass (up from 1486). README, the design spec and the implementation plan were updated, and a review-residual ledger was added.

**⚠️ This work is not review-clean.** The review hit its 10-round cap and emitted `UNRESOLVED`. Residual ledger: `docs/agent/reviews/2026-11-02-label-based-discovery-residuals.md` (currently untracked — it ships with the branch).

| Severity | Open finding | Status |
|---|---|---|
| HIGH | Cancellation reason must match `download error: download cancelled by user` (round 9 used bare equality, so real Ctrl+C was counted as a failure) | fixed after the last reviewer pass — **not independently re-reviewed** |
| MEDIUM | `--since` identity rescue must not be satisfied by a release of an unwanted type | fixed, **not re-reviewed** |
| MEDIUM | `SelectionCounts` doc described the pre-fix collapse behaviour | fixed, **not re-reviewed** |
| MEDIUM | No test bound the cancellation predicate to the real reason text | fixed, **not re-reviewed** |
| LOW ×2 | Label loop attributes a simultaneous budget/cancel stop differently from the artist sweep | **not fixed** (deliberate) |

**Unverified-fix gap:** round 10's fixes were applied after both reviewers finished reading the code. `QA_GATE_STATUS: CLEAN` covers lint, format, tests, coverage (97.51% lines), audit/policy and pre-commit on the final tree — it does not substitute for a reviewer reading round 10's diff.

**Version:** `0.33.1`. A release option would bump it (this is new backward-compatible functionality → MINOR, `0.34.0`), following the repo's `0.32.0` / `0.33.0` feature-release pattern.
